xray.one_line: A payments and shopping company whose OpenAI-powered assistant answers most of its customer-service chats, with humans brought back as a choice.
xray.what_it_does: Klarna is a payments and shopping company (it describes itself as a global digital bank and flexible payments provider) whose app lets consumers pay later, manage payments and shop. Since February 2024 its OpenAI-powered AI assistant has answered customer-service chats in the app, handling refunds, returns, payment issues, cancellations, disputes and invoice inaccuracies; Klarna says it handled 80% of customer-service chats in 2025. Customers can still ask for a human, and in May 2025 the CEO said Klarna would recruit human agents so that a person is always available. [s1, s6, s3, s8, s9]

situations.title: 2024 to 2025: AI-first customer service, then humans back
reach: Customer-service chats in the Klarna app: two-thirds of chats in the first month (2.3 million conversations), 80% of chats in 2025, Klarna says
Refunds, returns, payment-related issues, cancellations, disputes and invoice inaccuracies
Each customer's outstanding balances, upcoming payment schedules, purchase power and spending limits
The hand-off to a person: customers can choose a live agent, and the US help page offers human support or a dedicated agent
The customer-service workforce: about 3,000 agents, mostly at outsourcing partners, which a spokesperson said would fall to about 2,300

Klarna's public and regulatory statements about the assistant: 700 then 853 agents' equivalent work, $39 million (2024) and about $59 million (2025) in cost savings, satisfaction on par with humans, all from Klarna's own measurements
asked_our_example: Klarna's stated policy: every user is told they are talking to a chatbot and can choose to speak with a human instead (Klarna, December 2024)
As a Klarna spokesperson put it in March 2024: more experienced and senior staff are still needed, with specialised training for complex or sensitive cases
The assistant resolves routine errands end to end; a change to a customer's money or payment terms is recorded with who decided it
gap: Disputes, refunds and invoice corrections sit in the same chat reach as routine questions; nothing public shows where the line to senior human staff for complex or sensitive cases was drawn.
The human path that contains the agent (the choice of a person) depended on a workforce that was shrinking while the assistant took more chats.
The evidence of success is Klarna's own: share of chats, resolution time and satisfaction from its chat logs and internal surveys, with no independent measurement in the public record.

situations.title: Shopping assistant: from recommendation to purchase
reach: Klarna's price database of 5.6 million products from thousands of stores, with stock, delivery and cashback information
The user's shopping preferences and habits (what they buy and when, brands they prefer), used for recommendations
A purchase made directly in the app with Klarna's flexible payment methods (Pay Later and Fair Financing are consumer credit)
Merchants' listings and customer reviews, summarised into an 'unbiased, AI-generated' pros and cons
asked_our_example: Help the user find and compare products with a neutral summary
The purchase, and any credit used for it, is the user's own decision, made outside the recommendation
gap: Recommendations built from the user's habits run straight into a purchase, possibly on credit, in the same chat flow.
Klarna calls the summaries unbiased, but nothing public shows how the ranking is evidenced to be independent of Klarna's merchant relationships.

situations.title: Kiki: internal answers across internal systems
reach: Who is asking: answers are personalised to the person and their team
Over 250,000 employee questions and Kiki's answers (about 2,000 a day)
Third-party AI tools employees use, where Klarna's own risk factors say confidential information could be disclosed
asked_our_example: Answer an employee from information that employee is already allowed to see
No confidential information leaves Klarna's systems through an AI tool
gap: Kiki answers across internal systems and personalises by asker; nothing public shows how its answers follow each employee's own access.

questions: Which errands can the AI assistant complete on its own (refunds, dispute outcomes, invoice corrections, payment changes), and which must go to a person before money or payment terms change?
How is a dispute or other complex or sensitive case detected in the chat and handed to experienced staff, and is that hand-off recorded?
The satisfaction and accuracy figures come from your own chat logs and surveys: are they broken down by case type, and has anyone outside Klarna measured them?
When the shopping assistant leads to a purchase on credit, what separates the recommendation from the credit offer, and how is the 'unbiased' summary evidenced?
How do Kiki's answers respect each employee's own access to internal systems?
incidents: 2025-05: Klarna's CEO told Bloomberg that cost-cutting in customer service had gone too far and produced 'lower quality', and that Klarna would recruit human agents (a freelance, remote pilot) so customers always have a person. A Klarna spokesperson said the company was still 'very much AI-first'. In July 2025 Klarna told the SEC the remark concerned human customer service, not AI-driven service, and had been misreported. [s8, s9, s10, s7]

2026-02: Documented risk: Klarna's annual report says generative AI, including in its customer-service chatbot, may create inaccurate, incomplete or misleading output that may not be easily detectable. [s6]

help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Klarna's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
